title: Python Database Basics
intro: Python database connectivity interview questions for freshers connect the SQL knowledge you have to the Python code that executes it. This page covers the four steps every database operation follows in Python (connect → cursor → execute → fetch/commit → close), the sqlite3 standard library module as the no-setup-required starting point, the parameterised query pattern (%s or ? placeholders — the single most important concept in this module because it prevents SQL injection), why you must never use f-strings or string concatenation to build SQL queries (the SQL injection explanation that every interviewer loves to ask a follow-up about), psycopg2 as the PostgreSQL adapter and how its API mirrors sqlite3, and the ORM concept (SQLAlchemy or Django ORM as a Python-object layer above raw SQL — you don't need to be an ORM expert at fresher level, but you need to know it exists and why).
